ideas.title: Full-box, time-conditioned pointwise net for d-dimensional problems (Deep-Kolmogorov-style)
ideas.gap: JCP2024 trains only on a 1-D segment at tau = 0 even for d = 5/100; the net never sees the box or other times. Poseidon's time-conditioned layers and the deep Kolmogorov single-sample loss show that training on (t, x) sampled over the whole domain is the standard way to get a usable whole-space surrogate.
ideas.hypothesis: With states sampled in the full box and tau in (0, T), the kept R5a net (scaled I/O, gelu, 6x64) fits u(t, x) on Allen-Cahn d = 5 and the HJB d = 100 (Cole-Hopf exact) to the same L1 as the 1-D slice, and evaluation off the slice exposes the slice-trained net's failure.

rationale.novelty: Deep Kolmogorov / DBwD already train over boxes; applying it to coding-tree labels for fully nonlinear PDEs with time conditioning is a modest extension.
rationale.impact: Any downstream operator or control use needs the whole box, not a slice; every later direction builds on this data interface.
rationale.effect: Turns a slice surrogate into a whole-domain one at the same accuracy; material, not a step change.

ideas.title: Parametric-family conditioned net: (t, x, theta) -> u and policy derivatives for Merton / Merton-Vasicek
ideas.gap: One trained net per parameter set; a trader wants the value and the optimal policy (from u_x, u_xx) across gamma, sigma, mu, rate parameters at once. Berner-Grohs-Jentzen learned parametric Kolmogorov families from MC; nobody has done it for the fully nonlinear Merton HJB with branching labels.
ideas.hypothesis: A FiLM- or hypernetwork-conditioned MLP trained on 500-2000 theta instances x 1000 states each (each instance costs ~10 s of MC) reaches per-instance R5a accuracy on held-out theta and gives policies pi*(t, x; theta) from autograd derivatives, with the closed-form Merton/Vasicek solutions as referee.

rationale.novelty: Parametric operator learning from branching MC labels for a fully nonlinear HJB is a specific new combination; conditioning mechanisms are standard.
rationale.impact: The finance deliverable of the FYP: one surrogate for a family of portfolio problems, with policies.
rationale.effect: Amortises training over the family; accuracy target = per-instance level, so the gain is cost and coverage, not accuracy.

ideas.title: Terminal-condition operator learning: phi -> u(t, .) with DeepONet / FNO / attention operators on coding-tree labels
ideas.gap: Neural operators (DeepONet, FNO, GNOT/Transolver-type attention operators) learn maps between function spaces from PDE-solver data; all published ones use grid solvers for linear/semilinear PDEs in low d. No operator has been trained on branching-Monte-Carlo labels for fully nonlinear PDEs with arbitrary-order derivative terms, where grid solvers are unavailable in d > 3.
ideas.hypothesis: For a phi-family with analytic derivatives (random Fourier / GP samples with chosen smoothness), coding-tree labels on 2000-10000 phi instances suffice to train an operator G: phi -> u(t, .) whose held-out error matches per-phi R5a nets, at < 1/10 the per-new-phi cost; comparing DeepONet, FNO (1-D grid) and a cross-attention operator on identical data tells which backbone the MC-label regime favours.

rationale.novelty: Combination of existing operator architectures with a new label source (branching MC for fully nonlinear PDEs); the architectures are not new.
rationale.impact: Makes the fully nonlinear class amortisable: one operator per PDE, any terminal condition; the class that has no grid solver in high d.
rationale.effect: Baseline: one MC run + one net per phi (minutes). Target: milliseconds per new phi at equal accuracy after a one-off training; a step change in the cost regime if held-out error holds.

evidence: arXiv:2302.14376 GNOT; arXiv:2511.06294 Transolver is a linear transformer (2025); arXiv:2607.24513 Physics Transformer (2026) -- attention operators with arbitrary query points

feasibility.reason: The mechanism table depends on f only, so phi-instances cost only the lazy derivative lambdification (~ms for Fourier-series phi) plus MC; 1-D reference solutions via finite differences or high-M MC; 8 GB GPU is enough for DeepONet/FNO/attention operators of <= 20 M parameters.
feasibility.first_test: Linear heat equation (exact u = heat kernel * phi) with 500 random Fourier phi: if a DeepONet cannot reach L1 1e-3 on held-out phi from MC labels, the label noise / phi-family design is the bottleneck before any nonlinear problem is attempted.

ideas.title: Set-to-field Monte Carlo denoiser: attention over scattered noisy estimates, trained Noise2Noise across PDE instances
ideas.gap: Every deep-branching net is trained from scratch on one PDE's noisy point estimates and learns nothing transferable about how MC noise looks. Graphics denoisers (Noise2Noise, nonlinear N2N 2025) show a network can learn to denoise MC output from noisy targets alone, unbiasedly under MSE. No such denoiser exists for PDE-solution estimates.
ideas.hypothesis: A transformer that takes a set {(t_i, x_i, y_i, stderr_i)} of noisy coding-tree estimates (plus PDE/theta tokens) and answers queries (t, x) -> u, trained across thousands of cheap instances with Noise2Noise targets (independent second MC draw) or exact labels where available, reaches the accuracy of a per-instance net trained on 10x more samples; i.e. a 10x MC-budget reduction at deployment.

rationale.novelty: Noise2Noise + set/cross-attention are known; applying them to branching-MC PDE estimates as a learned, transferable estimator is a new combination.
rationale.impact: Applies to every coding-tree problem: the sampler stays unchanged, the denoiser sits on top.
rationale.effect: Baseline: per-instance R5a net at budget M. Target: same L1 at M/10 on held-out instances; a step change in sampling cost if it holds, and the heavy-tail regime (gotchas 15/20) is where it could fail.

evidence: arXiv:2512.24794 Nonlinear Noise2Noise for efficient Monte Carlo denoiser training (Dec 2025): noisy-target training is unbiased for MSE; nonlinear target maps bias it
arXiv:2302.14376 GNOT / arXiv:2511.06294: cross-attention from context points to query points

feasibility.reason: Data are unlimited and cheap (an instance-state set costs seconds); exact labels exist for AC/exp/Merton/HJB families for a clean first test; the user has built a transformer denoiser before; models of 5-20 M parameters fit an 8 GB GPU.
feasibility.first_test: Allen-Cahn d = 1 with T and the wave offset varied: train on 2000 instances at M = 1e3; if the denoiser's held-out L1 is not below a per-instance R5a net trained at M = 1e3 on the same states, there is no transferable structure to exploit and the direction stops.

ideas.title: Time-autoregressive backbone (semigroup / patch stepping) with certified patch length
ideas.gap: The single-shot tree estimator has infinite variance beyond T ~ 1 (gotcha 31); the authors' time patching is hand-tuned; Poseidon-style semigroup training and latent flow-matching solvers (2503.22600) treat time stepping as the learned object.
ideas.hypothesis: A recurrent/transformer stepper u(t+h, .) -> u(t, .) trained on tree labels with h below the L2 horizon from the estimator-integrity programme reaches T = 2 on Allen-Cahn with error growing linearly in the number of patches.

rationale.novelty: Patching exists (deep_branching_with_domain); a certified patch length and a learned stepper are new in combination.
rationale.impact: Extends the usable horizon of the whole method.
rationale.effect: Reaches horizons the single-shot method cannot, but the authors' hand-tuned patching already does; the gain is a guarantee plus a better backbone.

ideas.title: Diffusion / flow-matching model of the tree-functional distribution for uncertainty quantification
ideas.gap: Generative PDE solvers (DiffusionPDE, particle-guided diffusion 2026, PerFlow) model solution distributions; the coding-tree functional H has a heavy-tailed law that the mean-regression net discards.
ideas.hypothesis: A conditional flow-matching model of H | (t, x) reproduces the tail index from the estimator-integrity programme and gives calibrated intervals for u.

rationale.novelty: Generative modelling of branching-estimator laws is unexplored.
rationale.impact: Diagnostic only; the solution itself is a mean and is better estimated directly.
rationale.effect: No accuracy or cost gain for u; uncertain UQ benefit over the existing heavy-tail analysis.

ideas.title: Derivative-informed (Sobolev) training of the operator with DxN-rooted tree labels
ideas.gap: The sampler gives unbiased labels for any partial derivative of u by rooting trees at DxN(mu) (gotcha 25d); derivative-informed operator learning (Noguer 2026; Sobolev training) uses such labels to cut error on the derivatives that matter (policies, Greeks).
ideas.hypothesis: Adding u_x and u_xx labels to D02/D03 training reduces policy error by 2x at equal MC cost.

rationale.novelty: Prior-art overlap (Candidate 5 of the integrity programme; Czarnecki 2017; Huge-Savine 2020; Noguer 2026).
rationale.impact: Policies and hedges are derivatives; this is where finance accuracy is needed.
rationale.effect: 2x on derivative error is the published order of gain.

ideas.title: Multi-level Monte Carlo training: mixing cheap low-M and rare high-M labels for operators
ideas.gap: MLMC training of neural operators (2025) shows gradient estimates from a hierarchy of label fidelities cut data cost; coding-tree labels have a natural fidelity ladder (M) and a known variance model (stderr).
ideas.hypothesis: For D03/D04 training, an MLMC schedule over M in {1e2, 1e3, 1e4} reaches the accuracy of uniform M = 1e4 at 3x less MC work.

rationale.novelty: MLMC training exists for grid-solver operators; for branching MC with per-state variance it is a natural, specific extension.
rationale.impact: Reduces the dominant cost of every data-hungry direction (D02-D04).

ideas.title: Foundation-style pretraining across (f, phi, theta) families with an operator transformer for fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs
ideas.gap: PDE foundation models (Poseidon, DPOT, MORPH 2025, PDE-Transformer) pretrain on fluid-dynamics grids; none covers fully nonlinear parabolic PDEs with derivative nonlinearities or learns from Monte Carlo labels. The coding-tree sampler can generate that corpus.
ideas.hypothesis: A 20-50 M parameter operator transformer pretrained on ~1e4 instances spanning nonlinearity families (polynomial, exp, HJB-type), phi families and parameters, fine-tunes to a new PDE with 10x fewer labels than training from scratch (D03).

rationale.novelty: Foundation-model recipe applied to a new PDE class and label source; the recipe is not new.
rationale.impact: Would make the fully nonlinear class -- unreachable by grid solvers in high d -- a fine-tuning target; broad if it works.
rationale.effect: 10x label efficiency is Poseidon's reported order; uncertain here.
